I find it kinda sad that /v/gaming nowadays is almost exclusively used by people who want to promote their own website or YouTube channel. There is no sense in having a subverse if the only users on it use it as an advertising platform, and I think this kind of behavior is at very partially responsible for the reduced user activity on this subverse. Though there are some users who go out of their way to share actual video game news or interesting footage (props to @killer7 and @ChillyHellion), it's very annoying to click on "New" only to see that some seven out of ten posts are crap like "OVERWATCH: LE EPIC KILLSTREAK XDDD", all of whom are submitted by accounts with a very low submission contributions points and zero or nigh-empty comment contribution points.

I won't claim that I know how to fight the self-shilling. Some subverses have rules which prohibit posting content from the same source more than X times, but that is easily circumvented by copypastaing links to other sources to keep your own website there (see Trendie.com on /v/news). Perhaps the number of shills is the result of shrinking userbase because Voat increasingly turns into Stormfront: Reddit Edition. But I nonetheless would like to be able to browse /v/gaming without invariably being flooded by the same ten or so people who solely use the subverse to get clicks for their website or YouTube channel.

Suggestion. Start reporting these as spam. Anyone can post to v/ReportSpammers, as is encouraged to do so. There it's reviewed by Cynabuns, and if deemed a rule violation, either the user will be notified and given a chance to correct the situation ... or sent directly to Puttitout for action. Self-promotion is spam, as defined in Voat faqs, if it doesn't meet the following definition, see below:

Voat Faqs

Can I submit links to sites I operate?

Submitting only links to sites you operate (or are associated with), without submitting other, unrelated links, is considered spamming. If you submit niche content (for example gaming videos from your own YouTube channel), you should create your own subverse and submit the content only to that subverse. If majority of the links you submit are to sites you are associated with, your domains may be globally banned from Voat. To be on the safe side, if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 5 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.
